title: Isolate stale L2 learning entries on Geneve overlay after peering failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer escalations: multiple Dedicated tenants observed transient cross-tenant reachability immediately following VPC peering flaps. Symptoms: brief ICMP/TCP reachability between tenant VMs, ARP broadcasts observed on unexpected VXLAN/Geneve VNIs, and sudden spike in L2 forwarding table size on affected nodes. Hypothesis: after a peering route withdrawal, our overlay L2 learning table retained stale remote MAC->VNI mappings for the affected remote subnets, causing packets to be forwarded into the wrong tenant overlay before control-plane cleanup completed. This ticket tracks triage, root cause, patch, test plan, and rollout for a production fix that ensures per-VNI learning entries are quarantined/evicted on remote route withdrawal or substantial peer churn.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two tenants A and B on Dedicated cluster with peered VPCs over host-level Geneve overlay
2) Initiate traffic flow from A to B and confirm L2 learning entries populated on node N
3) Trigger peering flapping by toggling peer session (simulate route withdrawal) on the remote side
4) Observe brief period where node N forwards traffic for B into A's VNI and ARP broadcasts leak across VNI boundaries
5) Confirm that control-plane route reconciliation finishes but overlay learning table retained stale entries until NAT/time-based TTL expired (race window).
root_cause: Overlay dataplane (Geneve) learning table lacked a reliable invalidation path tied to control-plane remote route withdraw events. When a peer session reset occurred, L2 entries learned from the removed remote were not proactively evicted for the affected VNI, resulting in a transient window where encapsulated packets matched stale MAC->VNI bindings and were delivered across tenant boundaries.
proposed_fix: Add control-plane hooks to emit VNI-scoped flush events when a remote subnet/route withdraw is processed
On dataplane apply path, perform a VNI-scoped eviction of MAC/VTEP entries learned from that remote next-hop instead of relying solely on TTL-based expiry

Introduce a short-term read-through quarantine: if a packet matches a MAC->VNI mapping older than X seconds and the remote route changed in last Y seconds, drop and increment a metric to detect regressions
Unit and integration tests to simulate peering churn and assert no cross-VNI forwarding during/after route withdraw
Patch distributed rollout with 10% canary then 50% then full cluster once metrics validate.
testing_plan: Automated nightly integration test that simulates peering flaps and validates zero cross-tenant L2 reachability
Load test at scale: create 1k VNIs with churn and verify eviction latencies under load
Customer repro runbook for affected customers and test key scenarios in staging dedicated environment
Add Grafana dashboards: vni_flush_rate, stale_entry_drops, quarantine_drops, learning_table_size_by_node
rollout_plan: 2) Deploy to a small canary fleet for 24h and monitor quarantine_drops and customer error rates
3) Expand to 50% after 48h if no regressions, then to full cluster on maintenance window
4) If unexpected regressions, rollback by disabling feature flag and apply mitigation config that reduces learning TTL to 30s as temporary measure
